newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends down sharply, Dec at 6-month low.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends down sharply, Dec at 6-month low.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended down sharply Tuesday, as speculative liquidation of long positions drove the most-active December contract to its lowest settlement in six months, traders said.
"There was a lot of weak longs getting out of the market," one trader said.

December cocoa settled down $21 a tonne, at $1,361, its lowest level since March 29, after ranging between $1,390 and $1,360. Spot September fell $8, to $1,321, while the back months closed $15 to $21 lower.
Fund liquidation has battered the market the last four consecutive sessions, with December sliding $74 a tonne since last Wednesday's close, or about five percent.

Fueling the market's downturn has been unconfirmed reports that a private forecaster raised its 1996/97 Ivorian crop estimate as high as 900,000 tonnes. Earlier assessments came in around 800,000 to 850,000 tonnes.

"There are a lot of rumors, but nothing conclusive," one trader said. He said while the market's short-term outlook would depend on the updated Ivory Coast crop reports, in the long-term market fundamentals, such as strong grind figures, remained constructive.
Technically, traders pegged December support at $1,350, with the subsequent level seen at $1,340-$1,341.
